Pulmonary volumes represent discrete quantities of air inspired or expired under specific respiratory efforts.

Step 2: Evaluation
Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a maximal, forceful expiration (approximately 1100 mL to 1200 mL). This residual gas prevents complete collapse of alveoli and maintains continuous gas exchange between breaths. Expiratory reserve volume, inspiratory reserve volume, and tidal volume are completely or partially exhaled during forced expiration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Alveoli do not collapse after forceful expiration due to the Residual Volume.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q132 - Non-polymeric biomolecule class

questiontext.text: Which of the following are not polymeric ?

Biopolymers are macromolecular structures composed of repeating monomeric subunits linked by covalent bonds.

Proteins (polymers of amino acids), nucleic acids (polymers of nucleotides), and polysaccharides (polymers of monosaccharides) are true biological macromolecules. Lipids are esters formed between fatty acids and alcohols (e.g., glycerol) with molecular weights under 800 Da; they aggregate into supramolecular structures but are not true chemical polymers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Lipids are non-polymeric biomolecules.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q133 - Pollination agent for single ovule inflorescence flowers

questiontext.text: Flowers which have single ovule in the ovary and are packed into inflorescence are usually pollinated by

generalfeedback.text:

Pollination syndromes reflect floral adaptations tuned to specific abiotic or biotic transport vectors.

Step 2: Evaluation
Anemophilous (wind-pollinated) flowers are characterized by reduced perianth parts, single-ovule ovaries, and dense packing into inflorescences (e.g., corn, grasses). This architecture enables efficient capture of light, dry, wind-borne pollen grains over large air currents. Animal-pollinated flowers (bees, bats) typically feature larger nectar rewards and multiple ovules.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Flowers with single-ovule ovaries packed in inflorescences are adapted for wind pollination.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q134 - Life cycles of Ectocarpus and Fucus

questiontext.text: Life cycle of Ectocarpus and Fucus respectively are

Algal species display variable patterns of alternation of generations across their life cycles.

Ectocarpus (a filamentous brown alga) features an alternation of isomorphic haploid and diploid generations, exhibiting a haplodiplontic life cycle. In contrast, Fucus (a brown seaweed) possesses a dominant multicellular diploid plant body where meiosis yields haploid gametes directly, exhibiting a diplontic life cycle.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The life cycles of Ectocarpus and Fucus are haplodiplontic and diplontic, respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q135 - Biome exhibiting well defined vertical stratification

questiontext.text: Presence of plants arranged into well defined vertical layers depending on their height can be seen best in

generalfeedback.text:

Stratification refers to the vertical partitioning of vegetation into distinct height storeys based on light availability and microclimate.

Step 2: Evaluation
Tropical Rain Forests exhibit the most elaborate multi-layered vertical stratification, comprising emergent trees, upper canopy, lower canopy, sub-canopy shrub layer, and ground forest floor vegetation. Temperate forests, savannas, and grasslands have fewer vegetation strata.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Well-defined vertical layering of plants is best developed in Tropical Rain Forests.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q136 - Primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants

questiontext.text: Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) is the primary CO\(_{2}\) acceptor in

generalfeedback.text:

In \(\text{C}_4\) photosynthetic pathways, primary carbon fixation is spatially separated from the Calvin cycle.

In \(\text{C}_4\) plants, phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)—a 3-carbon compound located in mesophyll cells—acts as the primary acceptor of atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\). The reaction is catalyzed by PEP carboxylase (PEPcase) to form oxaloacetic acid (OAA). In \(\text{C}_3\) plants, ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) is the primary \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) serves as the primary \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor in \(\text{C}_4\) plants.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q137 - Role of carotene and retinal in visual photopigments

questiontext.text:
Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene rich food

Vitamin A derivatives formed from carotene, along with retinal serving as the light-absorbing component derived from vitamin A, explain why good vision depends on carotene-rich food.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q145 - Breeding modes prevented by dioecy in plants

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q147 - Migration criterion of DNA fragments in agarose gel electrophoresis

The agarose gel matrix acts as a sieve; smaller DNA fragments encounter less steric hindrance and migrate faster and farther through the gel pores than larger fragments.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The distance migrated by a DNA fragment on an agarose gel is inversely proportional to its size; smaller fragments move farther.

The water potential of pure water is zero.

Step 2: Evaluation
The descending limb of Henle's loop is freely permeable to water but impermeable to electrolytes. Conversely, the ascending limb is impermeable to water but actively or passively reabsorbs electrolytes (\(\text{Na}^+\), \(\text{K}^+\), \(\text{Cl}^-\)) into the medullary interstitium. Thus, stating that the ascending limb is impermeable to water is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water.

answer.text: The descending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to electrolytes.
The ascending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water.
The descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water.
The ascending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to water.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q163 - Target organ and trophic hormones of GnRH

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q164 - Structural orientation facilitating stomatal aperture opening

questiontext.text: Which of the following facilitates opening of stomatal aperture?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Stomatal opening is driven by turgor pressure changes within guard cells combined with specialized cell wall microfibrillar orientation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cellulose microfibrils in guard cell walls are oriented radially rather than longitudinally. When guard cells absorb water and swell, this radial microfibrillar arrangement limits lateral expansion and forces the cells to curve outward, drawing the inner thick elastic cell walls apart and opening the pore. Decreased turgidity causes stomatal closure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Radial orientation of cellulose microfibrils in guard cell walls facilitates stomatal opening.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q165 - Genotypic and phenotypic ratios in ABO blood group cross

questiontext.text: The genotypes of a Husband and Wife are I\(^{\text{A}}\)I\(^{\text{B}}\) and I\(^{\text{A}}\)i. Among the blood types of their children, how many different genotypes and phenotypes are possible?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Husband's genotype: \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{B}}\) (Blood Group AB).
Wife's genotype: \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}i\) (Blood Group A).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
ABO blood groups are governed by co-dominant alleles \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\) and \(\text{I}^{\text{B}}\), and recessive allele \(i\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Genetic cross: \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{B}} \times \text{I}^{\text{A}}i\)
Gametes produced by husband: \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\) and \(\text{I}^{\text{B}}\).
Gametes produced by wife: \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\) and \(i\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Combining gametes yields progeny genotypes:
1. \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{A}}\) \(\rightarrow\) Phenotype: Blood group A
2. \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}i\) \(\rightarrow\) Phenotype: Blood group A
3. \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{B}}\) \(\rightarrow\) Phenotype: Blood group AB
4. \(\text{I}^{\text{B}}i\) \(\rightarrow\) Phenotype: Blood group B

Count of distinct genotypes = 4 (\(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{A}}\), \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}i\), \(\text{I}^{\text{A}}\text{I}^{\text{B}}\), \(\text{I}^{\text{B}}i\)).
Count of distinct phenotypes = 3 (Group A, Group AB, Group B).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The genetic cross yields 4 distinct genotypes and 3 distinct phenotypes in the progeny.

Halophytes are salt-tolerant plants adapted to saline coastal mangrove swamps.

Plants possessing pneumatophores and exhibiting vivipary are halophytes.

Prokaryotic cell division relies on binary fission without eukaryotic cell cycle phase compartmentalization.

Extremophilic prokaryotes possess specialized membrane lipid structures adapted to hostile physical conditions.

Archaebacteria thrive in extreme saline conditions.

generalfeedback.text:

Myelination insulates nerve axons, increasing action potential conduction velocity via saltatory conduction.

In the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS), myelin sheaths are formed by Schwann cells wrapping around individual axons. name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q177 - Chronological sequence of mitotic cell division events

questiontext.text: Which of the following options gives the correct sequence of events during mitosis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mitosis progresses continuously through defined phases: prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.

Step 2: Evaluation
The sequential mitotic steps are:
1. Chromatin condensation (Prophase)
2. Disassembly of nuclear membrane (Prometaphase)
3. Chromosomal alignment at equator (Metaphase)
4. Centromere division and sister chromatid segregation (Anaphase)
5. Nuclear reassembly and decondensation (Telophase)
(Note: Crossing over occurs during meiotic prophase I, not in mitosis).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is Condensation \(\rightarrow\) nuclear membrane disassembly \(\rightarrow\) arrangement at equator \(\rightarrow\) centromere division \(\rightarrow\) segregation \(\rightarrow\) telophase.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q178 - Genetic disorder caused by autosomal primary non-disjunction

questiontext.text: A disease caused by an autosomal primary non-disjunction is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Non-disjunction during meiotic gametogenesis results in numerical chromosomal abnormalities (aneuploidies).

Step 2: Evaluation
Down's syndrome is caused by non-disjunction of autosomal chromosome pair 21 during gametogenesis, producing trisomy 21 (\(2n + 1 = 47\)). Down's syndrome is caused by autosomal primary non-disjunction.

Intestinal crypts contain specialized secretory cells contributing to digestive and mucosal innate defense functions.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q180 - Ex-situ biodiversity conservation strategy example

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is related to Ex-situ conservation of threatened animals and plants?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodiversity conservation strategies are categorized as in-situ (on-site in natural habitats) or ex-situ (off-site in artificial protected environments).

Step 2: Evaluation
Ex-situ conservation involves removing threatened or endangered species from wild natural habitats and placing them under human care in specialized facilities such as Wildlife Safari parks, zoological gardens, botanical gardens, and seed banks. Himalayan regions, biodiversity hotspots, and Amazon rainforests represent in-situ conservation habitats.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Wildlife Safari parks represent an ex-situ conservation strategy.
